payload.claim: `commit_squash` is passed `base_sha=base_sha` (the run's pin), which it prints verbatim as `base {base_sha[:12]}` in the squashed commit's own message (`saffron/phases/package.py:309`). For a stacked child this names a commit that is not the pushed commit's actual git parent (`target_head`), so the permanent audit line in the pushed history misdescribes what the patch was built on. Lower severity than the PR-body instance because it is buried in `git log` rather than shown to the reviewer directly, but it is the same wrong value reused a second time.
